generated_queries.text: Lesson objective: Students will retell major events and describe the central message of the story Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky through listening, discussion, role-play, and writing activities.

Students communicate clearly to present ideas, information, and texts aloud to audiences and peers using spoken language and sentence frames. Standard skill: present ideas information texts clearly in oral communication.

Students determine the meanings of unfamiliar words and concepts by applying knowledge of context and of academic vocabulary and word parts. Standard skill: use context and word parts to unlock unknown words.

Students make and track predictions about events and information likely to come next in a text based on titles, illustrations, and what they have already read. Standard skill: make and track predictions about upcoming events.
Students engage in dialogue with audiences by asking and answering questions during discussion and close read-aloud. Standard skill: ask and answer questions in oral dialogue with peers.

Students acquire and apply general, academic, and specialized vocabulary words and phrases through grade-level texts and content using word walls and oral practice. Standard skill: acquire and apply vocabulary from grade-level content.
Students refer to parts of texts when supporting an idea, answer, or opinion. Standard skill: use specific parts of texts to support ideas and answers.

Students describe characters, settings, and major events in a story using key details; describe traits of the main characters and how their words and actions support the central message of the story. Standard skill: describe story structure and character traits with details.
Students learn / practice: retell major events from a story
Students learn / practice: use text illustrations to support understanding of story events
Students learn / practice: participate in partner discussions to share and expand ideas
Students learn / practice: use sentence frames or prompts to support oral language production
Students learn / practice: role-play story events using puppets
Students learn / practice: write responses about story events and central message
Students learn / practice: self-assess learning using a protocol
Required student action — oral_production: participate in partner discussions, share ideas aloud, role-play story events, and self-assess learning orally
Required student action — written_production: write responses on the Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky response sheet
Required student action — matching_sorting_sequencing: sequence story events by placing icons on the Story Elements board and ordering story chunks
Required student action — procedural_application: apply the Sit, Kneel, Stand self-assessment protocol
Vocabulary targets (acquire / apply / clarify meaning): character, setting, moon, sun (L); sky, earth (T); The Sun, Moon, and Stars
Discussion Prompt: explain how story events support understanding of the central message and give examples
Reading Task: answer questions about story events and central message during read-aloud and discussions with partners and whole group; reflect on learning progress
Discussion Prompt: Invite students to sing and move along to the 'Sun, Moon, and Stars' song with you.

Discussion Prompt: 'What did you hear that helped you understand the important events from the beginning of the story?' (Sun wants Water to visit his and Moon's house, but Water says the house is too small for all of his people. Sun and Moon decide to build a larger house.)
